facts.text: Southeastern’s roots trace back to the early 1600s when English, Dutch, and Swedish explorers first charted the Delaware River, sparking the region’s colonial era.
The area that is now southeastern Pennsylvania is famously known as Pennsylvania Dutch Country, where Amish, Mennonite, and ‘Fancy Dutch’ communities still thrive.
Immigrants flocked to the Philadelphia region in the 1700s, drawn by booming manufacturing, publishing, textile, and railroad jobs that shaped the local economy.
Southeastern Pennsylvania spans ten counties—Berks, Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Lancaster, Lebanon, Lehigh, Montgomery, Northampton, and Philadelphia—each with its own unique history.
William Penn’s 1681 charter granted nearly all of present-day Pennsylvania, and his ‘Holy Experiment’ promised religious freedom that attracted English, Welsh, and Huguenot settlers.
